meta.title: OneAI Docs: Connect OneAI to Your Coding Agent | Hyperjump
meta.description: Route Claude Code, OpenCode, and other terminal coding agents through OneAI with one virtual key. Step-by-step setup for the Anthropic-compatible and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

index.heading: Connect OneAI to your coding agent
index.lede: Terminal coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenCode can send model requests to OneAI instead of a vendor API. You keep one virtual key, one budget, and your company's approved models inside the tools your engineers already use.
index.harnesses_heading: Pick the coding agent your team already uses
index.endpoints_heading: Pick the endpoint that matches your tool
index.endpoints_desc: OneAI exposes two compatible APIs. Anthropic-style tools use the /anthropic path, OpenAI-style tools use the /v1 path. Both accept the same virtual key.
index.security_heading: Keep the key out of your repository
index.security_text: Never commit a virtual key to git. Keep it in your shell profile, a secret manager, or the tool's own config file outside the repository. If a key leaks, revoke it in the OneAI console and create a new one.
index.cta_desc: Tell us which tool your team uses and we will write the setup guide for it.

mailto.subject: OneAI setup guide request
mailto.body:
Hi Hyperjump,

Our team uses ___ and would like a OneAI setup guide for it.

Company:
Name:
Tool:

Additional notes:

0.title: Open the OneAI console
0.text: Sign in as a User or Operator at {console}.

1.title: Name the key and set its limits
1.text: Open Virtual Keys from the navigation bar and choose Create New Virtual Key. Name the key so your team can recognize it, allow only the models it should call, and set the budget it may spend. A model that is not allowed cannot be called by the key.

2.title: Save the key now
2.text: The key is shown only at creation. Store it in your password manager. Treat it like a password: whoever holds it can spend your budget.

common.key_flow_note: If you lose the key, revoke it in Virtual Keys and create a new one. Never commit it to git.

claude_code.name: Claude Code
claude_code.summary: Anthropic's terminal coding agent. OneAI speaks the Anthropic Messages API, so Claude Code needs only an auth token, a base URL, and four model IDs.
claude_code.prerequisites: An active OneAI account, a Linux or macOS machine, and curl and bash installed.
claude_code.install_text: Run the official installer, then check that the binary is on your PATH.
claude_code.install_note: If the claude command is not found, restart your terminal or reload your shell profile with source ~/.bashrc or source ~/.zshrc.
claude_code.configure_text: Claude Code reads ANTHROPIC_* variables from the env block of ~/.claude/settings.json. Create the file if it does not exist and merge this block into it.
claude_code.configure_note: If settings.json already contains an env object, add these keys to it instead of replacing the whole file. Edit the file in your home directory, not the .claude/settings.json inside your project, which teams usually commit to git.

0.name: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
0.text: Your OneAI virtual key. OneAI authenticates on this variable, so no Anthropic API key is needed.

1.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
1.text: OneAI's Anthropic-compatible endpoint. Requests go to https://app.avenu.hyperjump.tech/anthropic.

2.name: ANTHROPIC_MODEL
2.text: Model for the main session. This is the model Claude Code uses for the work you ask it to do.

3.name: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL
3.text: Model behind the Opus alias. Claude Code uses it for Opus-tier requests and for planning in opusplan mode.

4.name: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL
4.text: Model behind the Sonnet alias. Claude Code uses it for Sonnet-tier requests and for execution in opusplan mode.

5.name: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL
5.text: Model behind the Haiku alias. Claude Code uses it for fast background work such as conversation titles and summaries.

claude_code.models_text: Model IDs use the provider path that OneAI exposes, for example default/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro. Every model ID you set must be allowed by your virtual key, otherwise the request fails with a model-not-allowed error. Keep the same ID in more than one variable if you want every tier to use the same model.
claude_code.verify_title: Check the base URL, then send a test prompt
claude_code.verify_text: Open a project directory, start Claude Code, and run /status. It must show https://app.avenu.hyperjump.tech/anthropic as the base URL. Any other URL means Claude Code is still talking to Anthropic, so fix the file before you continue. Then paste the test prompt below.
claude_code.verify_prompt: Reply with the single word READY and nothing else.
claude_code.verify_check: The reply alone does not prove which model ran, and a reply with no error proves nothing at all: a session still logged in to Anthropic replies just the same. Open LLM Logs in the OneAI console at {console} and read the newest request: it must be the prompt you just sent, its Provider column must say default, and its Model column must show one of the model IDs you configured. OneAI writes that log itself, so it is the authoritative check.

opencode.name: OpenCode
opencode.summary: An open-source terminal agent with a configurable provider registry. OneAI plugs in as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.
opencode.prerequisites: An active OneAI account, a Linux or macOS machine, and curl and bash installed.
opencode.install_text: Run the official installer, then check that the binary is on your PATH.
opencode.install_note: If the opencode command is not found, restart your terminal or reload your shell profile with source ~/.bashrc or source ~/.zshrc.
opencode.configure_text: OpenCode reads providers from the providers map in ~/.config/opencode/. Add the OneAI entry there, with your OneAI virtual key as the apiKey value. The block below is valid JSON, so it also works in opencode.json.
opencode.configure_note: Add the entry to the config file you already have in ~/.config/opencode/, opencode.json or opencode.jsonc, and create opencode.jsonc only if you have neither. Do not keep both files: when opencode.json and opencode.jsonc sit side by side, it is not clear which one OpenCode reads. If your file already lists providers, add OneAI next to them inside the providers map instead of replacing the file. The file now holds your virtual key, so keep it in your home directory, not in a project folder that teams usually commit to git.

0.name: package
0.text: The @opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible adapter. It lets OpenCode talk to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including OneAI.

1.name: name
1.text: Display name shown in the OpenCode model picker. Keep it as OneAI so the source is obvious.

3.name: settings.apiKey
3.text: Your OneAI virtual key. OpenCode sends this value as the API key on every request to OneAI. Keep opencode.jsonc out of version control, because it stores the key in plain text.

4.name: models
4.text: Model IDs you want to expose, each with a readable label. Add as many as your virtual key allows.

5.name: model
5.text: Top-level default model, written as provider/model. Here it selects oneai/default/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, so OpenCode starts on OneAI without a manual model pick.

opencode.verify_title: Check the provider, then send a prompt
opencode.verify_text: Start OpenCode and open the model picker. The selected model must be the OneAI model you set as the default, the entry that starts with oneai/. A model from another provider means OpenCode is not using the OneAI provider. The default model is already set, so no model picking is needed. Then paste the test prompt below.
opencode.verify_prompt: Reply with the single word READY and nothing else.
opencode.verify_check: The reply alone does not prove which model ran, and a reply with no error proves nothing at all: a session still pointed at another provider replies just the same. Open LLM Logs in the OneAI console at {console} and read the newest request: it must be the prompt you just sent, its Provider column must say default, and its Model column must show one of the model IDs you configured. OneAI writes that log itself, so it is the authoritative check.
